q1_needs_attention.curator_notes: Ranked by irreversibility, then time pressure, then counterparty weight. The press release edges out the bounced Tessa email because it is 16 days overdue against an Aug 15 external launch, while the bounce is recoverable the moment Jordan sees it. The Klaviyo price increase is kept in Q1 rather than Q5: the only message stating the old $14,400 rate is the same message announcing the new one. The lookalike-domain phishing note is included strictly as a hazard; any payable framing would be disqualifying. The Google sign-in alert is ranked high (not last): the attacker used the account's current, just-rotated password, and the account holds Klaviyo, Meta and Google Ads access, which makes it the most irreversible item in the set if ignored. The Fold & Field retainer counter (Jordan waiting on Tessa) was removed from this question — Jordan has already acted and her own next step is gated on Tessa's reply, which is a Q4 chase-list shape, not a Q1 attention item; it remains in Q4. The DTC Growth Summit booking is a genuine agreed-to commitment buried in promotional-category mail; note that a differently-named, differently-domained 'DTC Summit' (dtcsummit.co) declined an Oct 14 panel back in June — the corpus never states whether these are the same event, so gold treats them as two separate organizations rather than inventing a resolution.

q2_forgetting.curator_notes: Q2 vs Q6 was decided by the engagement test: everything here is attested by Jordan's own SENT or DRAFT text. The Alan contract promise and the Amara-is-waiting item in Q3 are one chain but two obligations (draft to legal, contract to creator) and are scored in different questions, not twice in one. Two corpus-wide contradictions bear on items here and are recorded rather than resolved: (1) the replatform go-live date is stated as both Aug 17 (Nina, Jul 8; Sofia, Aug 5) and Sept 1 (Jordan's own Jul 21 and Aug 10 messages) — marketing-q2-01's claim states this plainly instead of picking a winner; the equivalent Q5 item (marketing-q5-06) has been moved to borderline for the same reason. q3_waiting_on_me.curator_notes: Every item here has a named human (or a person's workflow) whose next step depends on Jordan, and in each case the counterparty spoke last. The press release resend is one item with elevated urgency, never two. q6_slipping_through_cracks.curator_notes: Every item passes both tests: real consequence plus a burial factor (bounce, attachment-only, quote-only, misleading subject, auto-responder, bcc, or promotional-category filing). Four items from the earlier draft did not survive a full-mailbox re-check and were moved to must_not_include: the fall studio day did not 'die in an auto-responder' — Jordan re-sent logistics the next day in a parallel thread and got a substantive reply; the Fold & Field retainer negotiation is loudly attested across roughly five correctly-titled threads and fails the burial test outright; and both typo'd-address bounces (priyanka.rao@, hgrant@) are annotated in the corpus itself as harmless mistypes that were resent correctly, with no evidence anything was lost. The bcc item (marketing-q6-10) is retiered to borderline: the specific decision window it warns about closed five weeks before the as-of date and the number it discusses was independently reconfirmed elsewhere, so the structural blind spot is real but nothing is currently at risk from it. The hardest call remains Amara's unsigned photo usage addendum: Jordan wrote both messages herself and chased once, which a strict reading of the engagement test pushes toward Q2/Q4, but six weeks of total silence during an active renegotiation with the same counterparty reads as a real orphaning, so it stays here. The Google Ads item is deliberately scoped to only the one confirmed Google disapproval (b40f18c2e4b60024); an earlier draft of this finding cited a second 'disapproval' that was actually a separate Meta ad rejection on a different platform, which does not actually compound toward Google's own policy-standing warning — that conflation has been dropped.
